summary: Korea is a memory chip market, and it swings hardest on AI news. SK hynix's record quarter lifted the KOSPI 6.63% on Oct 28, but on Oct 29 Samsung's record profit of 107.44 trillion won only matched estimates and it put off new shareholder returns until January, so its shares fell 4.13% and the KOSPI 1.24% to 5,937.66 (CNBC, TradingKey). Samsung says HBM is sold out for next year and chip markets stay tight through 2028, and it will raise chip capex 62% (Reuters). The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% on Oct 22 and says more hikes depend on Q3 GDP and inflation. US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, the SK hynix ADR (SKHY), Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.
for_you: No chase. EWY closed at 165.91 on Oct 28, up 5.37%, and SKHY at 164.70, up 13.3% (Massive), before Seoul gave back part of the gain. MU, the US memory name, rose on 1.19 times volume, not a confirmed breakout. Korean bank ADRs (KB, SHG) stay mixed.

watch.name: KOSPI
watch.why: Down 1.24% as Samsung fell 4.13% on no new payout plan; SK hynix rose 2.22% (TradingKey).

watch.name: Bank of Korea base rate
watch.why: Held unanimously after July and August hikes. Governor Shin says more hikes depend on Q3 GDP and inflation; most watchers expect two more through next year.

watch.name: Won per US dollar
watch.why: Fourth straight daily gain and strongest since Oct 2, 2024 (Aju Press). A stronger won eases inflation and the case for more hikes.

watch.name: Foreign net buying
watch.why: Foreign investors were net buyers on Oct 21 while retail investors sold about 1.13 trillion won (Aju Press).

changes.what: The KOSPI fell 2.62% to about 6,626 as foreigners kept selling Samsung and SK Hynix, each down about 2.4%. Profit taking in memory chips is driving Korea lower.

The KOSPI fell 3.65% to 6,384.24, its lowest close since Aug 11, as foreigners sold a net 2.02 trillion won for a tenth straight day. Samsung fell 4.39% and SK Hynix 4.52%, and China's CXMT said a new memory platform is in mass production.
changes.for_you: No action. Korean bank ADRs fall with foreign outflows; avoid new buys before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. The same memory selloff hit MU premarket, so skip memory swings for now.

changes.what: The KOSPI fell about 6% on Oct 13, below 6,000 for the first time since August, and a sell sidecar paused program selling. SK Hynix fell about 8.5% and Samsung about 6.8%, with SK Square down about 12%.
changes.for_you: No action except to stay out. EWY fell 4% Monday and has more to digest; MU is not a setup. Watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: Correction and update: the KOSPI closed Oct 13 at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, not below 6,000 (that was intraday). SK Hynix closed down 10.09% and Samsung 7.39%. On Oct 14 an early rebound of over 2% faded and the index closed down 0.44% at 6,008.81, its sixth straight loss, with Samsung up 0.65% and SK Hynix down 1.66%.
changes.for_you: No action. A failed bounce is a sign the selling is not done, so no MU or memory swings. KB, SHG and WF stay hurt; watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: The KOSPI plunged 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15 ('Black Thursday'), its seventh straight loss, with a sell side sidecar at 9:07am and a Level 1 circuit breaker at 12:38pm. SK hynix fell about 11% to 1,262,000 won and Samsung about 9.5% to 210,000 won. Analysts cited AI return doubts, China's CXMT and US rate hike risk.
changes.for_you: No action. Do not sell puts on EWY or MU into this; rich premiums reflect real risk. Korean banks stay hurt into the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. CPNG is left out because its business is retail, not chips.

changes.what: The KOSPI bounced on Oct 16 after the 7.57% crash: AP had it up about 2.1% at 5,668.05 early, and Saxo later reported a 4.11% gain to 5,782.62, with Samsung and SK hynix steadying. The close was not confirmed at writing.
changes.for_you: No action. One up day after a 7.6% crash is not a bottom, so EWY and MU are in neither list. Wait for SK hynix (Oct 28) and Samsung (Oct 29) results before any memory trade. EWY closed Oct 15 at 156.22, down 11% in a month.

changes.what: The KOSPI closed Oct 16 up 2.05% at 5,668.06 but lost 14.46% for the week, its biggest weekly drop since October 2008 (TradingKey). Samsung closed at 215,500 won (up 2.62%) and SK hynix at 1,272,000 won (up 0.79%). In New York EWY fell 3.7% to 150.44 the same day as US chip stocks sold off again (dashboard).
changes.for_you: No action. A 14% week is forced selling; wait for SK hynix on Oct 28 before any Korea or memory trade. Korean bank ADRs stay hurt into the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. CPNG is left out: its business is retail, not chips.

changes.what: Two surveys published Oct 18 expect the Bank of Korea to hold its 3.00% rate on Oct 22: 19 of 20 experts in a Seoul Economic Daily poll and all 11 in a MoneyToday poll. Most expect a 'hawkish hold' and another hike in November, sooner if the Fed signals a December hike.
changes.for_you: No action. A hold removes Thursday's surprise risk, but a November hike stays on the table, so Korean bank ADRs (KB 118.81, SHG 70.31) stay hurt. Wait for SK hynix on Oct 28 before any Korea or memory trade.

changes.what: The KOSPI rose 1.8% to 5,768.01 on Oct 19 (AP) after the worst week for Samsung and SK hynix since 2008; it is still down more than 17% in a month. Foreign investors sold about 11.2 trillion won ($7.8 billion) of KOSPI stocks last week, and foreign ownership of Samsung fell to 45.98% on Oct 16, the lowest since July 2009 (Seoul Economic Daily).
changes.for_you: No action. One up day after a 14% weekly drop is a bounce. EWY (150.44) had up/down volume 0.93 on Friday. Korean bank ADRs stay hurt into Thursday's rate decision.

changes.what: Seoul sold the AI rebound on Oct 20: the KOSPI was down 2.8% at 5,607.95 early (AFP) and about 3.65% later in the session, below 5,600, with SK hynix and Samsung leading. Elice, an AI data center firm, fell about 30% on its Kosdaq debut despite retail demand over 400 times the shares offered (Seoul Economic Daily, TechNode). Closing levels were not confirmed at writing.
changes.for_you: No action. Korean bank ADRs KB (118.81) and SHG (70.31, Oct 16 closes) stay hurt into Thursday's Bank of Korea decision. A failed AI listing is one more sign lenders and buyers are pulling back from data center bets.

changes.what: The KOSPI closed down 3.73% at 5,552.74 on Oct 20, its lowest close since April 7, then rose 3.29% to 5,735.66 on Oct 21 as foreigners bought a net 660 billion won; Samsung rose 5.67% and SK hynix 5.81%. The won firmed to 1,325.2 per dollar, and chip exports in the first 20 days of October rose 222.5% from a year ago.
changes.for_you: No action before the Bank of Korea decides tonight (9pm ET). KB and SHG are now mixed: a stronger won and the chip rebound help, a November hike risk cuts the other way. Only 372 stocks rose against 488 that fell, so this was a two stock rally, not a broad turn.

changes.what: The Bank of Korea held its rate at 3.00% on Oct 22 in a 7 to 0 vote but signaled more tightening, saying the timing of further hikes depends on Q3 GDP and inflation. The KOSPI fell 3.52% to 5,533.77, its lowest close since April, wiping out Oct 21's rebound as chip stocks sold off with US AI names.
changes.for_you: No action. KB and SHG are left out of both lists: higher rates help bank margins, but the market selloff and a weaker economy cut the other way.

changes.what: SK hynix halted the review of a pre IPO round and Nasdaq listing for its US NAND unit Solidigm, easing worries about a duplicate listing; the stock rose about 4.4% and lifted the KOSPI 0.30% to 5,550.30 on Oct 23 after an early 2.36% drop. Foreign investors were net sellers of 994.1 billion won. SK hynix reports Q3 before 9am Seoul time on Oct 28, which is 8pm ET on Oct 27.
changes.for_you: No action. The US listed Korea names are left out because the move was about SK hynix, which does not trade in the US. Its report Monday night US time is the first big memory read of the week.

changes.what: The KOSPI rose 3.09% to 5,638.34 on Oct 27, its biggest gain since February, after Anthropic's IPO filing lifted AI stocks; SK hynix rose 5.18% to 1,341,000 won and Samsung 4.23% to 222,000 won, and foreigners bought a net 592.9 billion won (Digital Today, MoneyToday). That reversed a 1.46% drop on Oct 26.
changes.for_you: No action. SK hynix reports at 8pm ET tonight; one day of buying before a report is not a trend. The US listed names are left out of both lists because the move was about the chip makers.

changes.what: SK hynix reported Q3 revenue of 104.6 trillion won and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won on Oct 28, both above estimates, and plans about 100 trillion won of shareholder returns; 14 customers signed long term deals covering more than 50% of its 2027 and 2028 capacity. Its shares rose 10.89% and the KOSPI 6.63% (CNBC).
changes.for_you: No action today. Do not chase the gap before the Fed and big tech results; Samsung reports Oct 29.

changes.what: Samsung reported record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, about in line, with chip profit of 106.5 trillion won; it said HBM is sold out for next year and chip capex rises 62%, but deferred new shareholder returns to January (CNBC, Reuters). Samsung fell 4.13%, SK hynix rose 2.22% and the KOSPI fell 1.24% to 5,937.66 (TradingKey).
changes.for_you: No action. Memory demand is confirmed by both makers; the stocks now trade on payouts. Do not chase EWY after a 5.37% day.
